article.description: Rookie reserve Nicole Powell scored 14 points and grabbed seven rebounds to lead the Charlotte Sting past the Indiana Fever 63-53 Wednesday night.
article.headline: Powell's 14 points, 7 boards lead Sting
article.linkText: Rookie Powell leads Sting past slumping Fever
article.story:
INDIANAPOLIS (AP) -- Rookie reserve Nicole Powell is starting to
feel comfortable in the WNBA.

The former Stanford star scored 14 points for the second
consecutive game Wednesday night and had seven rebounds to lead the
Charlotte Sting past the Indiana Fever 63-53.

"I'm just glad to be contributing," said Powell, who tied her
season-high in just 23 minutes. "I'm just trying to stay
consistent. We're halfway through the season, and I'm feeling
comfortable out there."

Allison Feaster and Tammy Sutton-Brown also had 14 points for
the Sting (12-11) as Indiana lost its fifth consecutive game.
Sutton-Brown also contributed six blocked shots.

Tamika Catchings led Indiana (12-14) with 13 points and eight
rebounds. No other Indiana player finished in double figures.

"We expected a motivated Indiana team to come out," Feaster
said. "We knew they'd have a big surge at the beginning. Once we
gained our composure, we were able to put it together. ... I
thought we worked hard at keeping the ball out of Catchings' hands.
We just tried to keep it mixed up defensively."

After trailing by 14 points early in the second half, the Fever
used an 11-0 run to take a 49-47 lead. Charlotte responded with
eight consecutive points to take the lead for good.

Sutton-Brown made two free throws to tie the game at 47 and then
hit a short jumper to put the Sting ahead to stay with 5:13 to go.
A layup by Powell, a steal and jumper by Feaster and two free
throws by Sutton-Brown made it 57-49 with 2:58 left.

Charlotte overcame a drab start to lead 29-19 at halftime after
holding the Fever to just one field goal in a 12-minute span. After
Indiana led 9-0, Charlotte put together a 20-3 run.

"With this team we always know we're not out of it. It was just
a matter of sticking with it and playing hard," Powell said.
"Tonight was a great example of what a team effort it was. We just
worked well together."

Charlotte took a 29-16 on a 3-pointer by Powell before a layup
by Natalie Williams ended Indiana's string of 11 consecutive
misses.

"It's very frustrating because we're a better team than how we
played," said Catchings, who was 5-of-17 from the field.

Charlotte frustrated Indiana when it switched to a zone defense
in the second half.

"We came back in the second half. Then they went zone and we
didn't handle it well," Indiana coach Brian Winters said. "We
competed hard in the second half, but we didn't do the little
things well."
